scheme_name: Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program in Horticulture Department HRT 5
description:
The Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program is a welfare initiative under the Horticulture Department of the Government of India. 

This scheme was launched in 2018 to enhance the income of farmers and promote the processing of fruits and vegetables. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to reduce post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables. 

It aims to provide training to farmers on various preservation techniques. 

The scheme also focuses on improving the quality of processed products. 

One of the measurable targets of this scheme is to train at least 50,000 farmers annually. 

The program encourages the establishment of small-scale processing units. 

Farmers are provided with technical knowledge to enhance their skills in horticulture. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for setting up processing units. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh as a subsidy for equipment purchase. 

This subsidy covers 50% of the total cost of the equipment. 

The scheme also provides training sessions that last for a duration of 10 days. 

During these sessions, farmers learn about various preservation methods. 

These methods include canning, bottling, and dehydration techniques. 

The training is conducted by experts from the Horticulture Department. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a resident of India. 

Farmers must be engaged in horticulture activities. 

There are no specific age limits for applicants. 

However, preference is given to small and marginal farmers. 

Income criteria are not strictly defined but farmers with lower incomes are prioritized. 

Educational qualifications are not mandatory for participation in the scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must visit the nearest Horticulture Department office. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the department. 

Farmers must submit documents proving their identity and land ownership. 

Aadhar card and land ownership documents are typically required. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the department officials. 

If approved, farmers are notified about the training schedule. 

The training sessions are usually conducted in local agricultural colleges or community centers. 

The frequency of training sessions is typically quarterly. 

Farmers can apply for the subsidy after completing the training program. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is processed within 30 days of application. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The Horticulture Department at the state level oversees the implementation. 

Farmers can contact the local Horticulture Department office for assistance. 

The contact details for the Horticulture Department can be found on the official state government websites. 

The scheme has been instrumental in reducing post-harvest losses by approximately 30%. 

This reduction translates to increased income for farmers involved in horticulture. 

The training program has also led to the establishment of over 5,000 small-scale processing units across the country. 

Farmers who have undergone the training report a 20% increase in their overall income. 

The scheme also promotes the use of organic methods in the preservation of fruits and vegetables. 

This aligns with the government's broader goal of promoting sustainable agriculture. 

The program has received positive feedback from participants. 

Many farmers have expressed satisfaction with the practical knowledge gained. 

The scheme also encourages women farmers to participate actively. 

Women constitute about 40% of the total beneficiaries of the program. 

The government aims to increase this percentage in the coming years. 

The scheme has provisions for follow-up training sessions. 

These sessions help farmers stay updated with the latest preservation techniques. 

The training also includes marketing strategies for processed products. 

Farmers learn how to package and sell their products effectively. 

The scheme has been linked with various other government initiatives. 

These include the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi and the National Horticulture Mission. 

By integrating with these programs, the scheme aims to provide comprehensive support to farmers. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme over five years. 

This budget is aimed at enhancing infrastructure and providing better training facilities. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is projected that around 1 lakh jobs will be created through this initiative. 

The training program is designed to be inclusive and accessible to all farmers. 

The government is committed to ensuring that no farmer is left behind. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the scheme. 

These assessments help in making necessary adjustments to improve the program. 

The scheme is part of a larger vision to double farmers' income by 2022. 

The government is focused on creating a robust horticulture sector in India. 

The Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program is a crucial step in this direction. 

It empowers farmers with knowledge and resources to thrive in the horticulture industry. 

The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to the overall economic growth of rural areas. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to enhance their livelihoods. 

The government continues to promote awareness about the scheme through various channels. 

This includes workshops, seminars, and online platforms. 

The aim is to reach as many farmers as possible and encourage their participation. 

In conclusion, the Scheme for Fruit and Vegetable Preservation and Training Program is a vital initiative. 

It provides essential support to farmers in the horticulture sector. 

With its comprehensive approach, the scheme aims to transform the landscape of fruit and vegetable processing in India.
